newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPG market firms for end-month barrels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPG market firms for end-month barrels.

text.p: U.S. liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices edged higher again in Tuesday's early session, mainly due to end-month propane and butane covering for the Mont Belvieu, Texas hub.

"There's a squeeze for the end-of-month on propane and probably still on butane (at Belvieu). Conway (Kansas hub) is trying to follow but there seems to be still plenty of supply up there," said a trader at a major in Oklahoma.
Propane at Belvieu was up about one cent a gallon at 41.00/41.25 cents/gallon in early afternoon trading, with Conway prices around 39.00/39.50 cents/gal.
Brokers in Texas said they expect propane there to ease back after deals as high as 41.50.

"There are plenty of barrels (in Conway) and there has been all month," said one trader, noting that the backwardation of around 1.25 cents into next month suggested the firmer prices were short-lived.
